One day, after listening for a long time to a conversation about leghorns, laces, jewellery and Parisian milliners and mantua makers, interspersed with many names of fashionable celebrity, in the course of which Nellie learned that one of the sisters had a dozen expensive hats the year previous, and the other an endless number and variety of mantles, and that neither thought a thousand dollars an extravagant price for a real India shawl — Nellie resolved to test the character of their religious sentiments.
